problem: Existing home-scale rearrangement benchmarks (Habitat 2.0 HAB) rely on magical grasp and slow CPU simulation, while low-level manipulation sims lack home-scale tasks; no benchmark unifies fast sim, realistic low-level control, baselines and controllable large-scale demo generation.
motivation: Frontier robot learning needs faster simulation, more intricate home-scale environments and large demonstration datasets. Realistic grasping and whole-body control make tasks much harder, and IL policies turn out to be sensitive to demonstration behavior, so data needs to be filtered by behavior and safety.
key_idea: Re-implement the Habitat Home Assistant Benchmark on GPU-parallel ManiSkill3 with realistic low-level whole-body control, train RL/IL skill baselines, and use simulator-privileged event labeling to filter demonstrations by behavior and safety.
insight: Per-object Pick/Place RL policies overfit to geometry and beat all-object policies mainly on varied objects (TidyHouse Pick +10.12 train) or tight tolerances (PrepareGroceries Place +6.85 to +7.04); on the Cracker Box, all-object policies fail far more to collisions and grasping. Easing collisions and place criteria still yields ≤20% task success, so low-level whole-body control is the main bottleneck. Filtering demos biases IL behavior (place:drop ratios shift) but does not fully control it.
method: GPU-accelerated HAB in ManiSkill3: Fetch mobile manipulator, ReplicaCAD scenes with handle collision meshes added, SequentialTask eval env plus per-subtask dense-reward training envs; 4096 parallel envs

Subtask skills with low-level control: Pick, Place, Open/Close Fridge/Drawer, each with success/failure conditions including cumulative collision force limits; navigation is replaced by teleport; perfect task planner chains skills

RL baselines: SAC for Pick/Place (50M/25M steps) and PPO for Open/Close, depth-image input with 3-frame stacking; per-object policies vs all-object policies; Place initialized from grasp poses sampled from Pick policies; 150 policies x 3 seeds

Automated event labeling and trajectory categorization: privileged events (Contact, Grasped, Dropped, Success, Excessive Collisions) ordered into lists mapped to mutually exclusive success/failure modes
Demo generation and IL baselines: 1000 filtered demos per object from per-object RL policies; BC (5-layer CNN + MLP) and Diffusion Policy baselines
Benchmarking: Interact benchmark vs Habitat 2.0 for SPS and GPU memory, plus ray-tracing comparison vs Behavior-1k

setting.backbone: SAC/PPO RL policies with small CNN encoders + MLPs (trained from scratch); BC and Diffusion Policy for IL
setting.training_data: Online RL in sim on HAB train split (10,000 episode configs per task); IL on 1000 filtered RL-generated demos per task/subtask/object
setting.observation: two 128x128 depth images (head and arm) + privileged GT target object pose/goal position/handle position, TCP pose, grasp indicator, proprioception
setting.action_space: low-level normalized [-1,1]: PD joint delta position for arm/torso/head, base linear and angular velocity; navigation by teleport
setting.privileged: GT object/goal/handle poses given to the policy; perfect task planner; teleport navigation; privileged sim info for trajectory labeling

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmark; results are subtask success-once rates and progressive completion rates (mostly in figures). Manipulation subtask numbers are in Table 1 but no canonical bench applies.
results: The environments reach 4299.18 SPS at 15.35 GB VRAM, 3.08x faster than Habitat 2.0 (1397.65 SPS at 22.60 GB) with 32% less VRAM. Per-object RL policies beat all-object and IL policies on subtasks (e.g. TidyHouse Pick val 77.48 vs 68.15 vs 59.03). Long-horizon completion remains low, and the Close Fridge policy gets 0% on val.
limitations: Baselines are far from solving long-horizon tasks; the optimistic upper bound is low, and skill handoffs and clutter disturbances cause loss
Navigation is teleported and policies use GT object poses; no real-robot transfer is claimed
Close Fridge fails on val scenes (fridge door opens into a wall), showing limited scene diversity; IL and DP baselines are weak on Pick
